messages.subject: effect sizes in MQM
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I ran mqmscan with mqm argument object and cofactors produced by
‘mqmsetcofactors’ function. I could detect significant 3 QTLs (LOD
scares were 5.6, 4.7 and 9.1) without any strong epistatic interaction
(checked in effectplot graphs), and would like to calculate their
effect sizes. I used fitqtl to calculate % variance but, since LOD
scores in the drop one QTL ANOVA table were much lower than I got in
MQM (2.4, 2.3 and 4.0, respectively), I wondered if these % variances
could not be right for QTLs detected in MQM.
I would appreciate it if you would advice the way of calc for effect
size in MQM if there is…
Thank you very much!
Best,
Masto

messages.body_plain:
The MQM functions and fitqtl use different methods of fitting a model, which could contribute to the difference.  Also, you'd maybe want to include all of the marker covariates that were used in the MQM scan.

karl

messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure I understand, but if you want to calculate the covariance between phenotypes, you could first pull out the phenotype data from a cross object:

  phe <- mycross$pheno

and then use var() or cor().

  var(phe)
  cor(phe)
  cor(phe[,1], phe[,2])

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Hypothesis testing under CIM
messages.body_plain:
The usual treatment of CIM is to compare the model with cofactors + QTL under test versus just the cofactors, where at any given position the cofactors within some window are excluded from each of the null and alternative.  This is what the LOD scores that come from cim() correspond to.  To establish significance, one would use a permutation test, including the selection of cofactors as part of the evaluation.

But I would encourage you to focus on the MQM code rather than the cim() function.  Even more, I would suggest focusing on the multiple-QTL model functions fitqtl(), addqtl(), stepwiseqtl(), etc.

Evaluating evidence for individual QTL in the context of a multiple-QTL model is not easy and should not be reduced to a series of hypothesis tests.

karl

messages.subject: MQM analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have been using R/qtl and MQM analysis to examine a number of
phenotypes in an F2 cross. Due to the computing time required for
calculating penalties for stepwiseqtl() I haven't used this function
much yet but I am planning to. I have also now been working with the
cofactor selection and mqmscan() calls in the newest tutorial. My
question is this: aside from the penalized LOD thresholds used in the
stepwiseqtl() algorithm what, if any, are the major differences
between these methods (especially calling makeqtl() and fitqtl() vs.
mqmsetcofactors() and mqmscan() )? I understand that cofactor
selections are automated with the latter method but is this any
different than running fitqtl() and then addqtl() and addint() and
"doing it by hand"?

messages.subject: Support for RILs
messages.body_plain:
I am working with a diploid RIL plant population and would like to use
R/QTL to analyze several phenotypes. Problem is my phenotypes have low
heritability and the environmental variance in my data is reasonably
high so I am uncomfortable averaging across biological reps
(individuals with the same genotype but potentially different
phenotypes) and reporting one average phenotype per unique genotype.

As far as I can tell, the last time this issue was brought up (at
least in this group) was almost 3 years ago (http://groups.google.com/
group/rqtl-disc/browse_thread/thread/557a06f51093d912/602bac304d1dd2ec?
lnk=gst&q=RIL#602bac304d1dd2ec) where it was mentioned that one can
encode each rep as a separate individual with an identical genotype,
but in that discussion I agree with Dr. Broman that such an
implementation is a poor work around as it inflates LOD scores and
makes it difficult to pin down a significance threshold.

I can't really find any documentation elsewhere on this issue. Has
there been any further updating to support the proper analysis of RIL
populations with multiple reps/genotype since 2008 in R/QTL? Are there
plans to implement this further in the future?

Thanks for the otherwise very robust and versatile platform!
JC

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM analysis
messages.body_plain:
There are differences in how the models are fit. (That is, how the missing genotype data at putative QTL is accommodated.). The other major difference concerns the evaluation of the quality of a model (or its terms).  MQM makes use of the estimated residual SD under a "full model" with all marker covariates, while fitqtl and related functions estimate the residual SD separately for each QTL model.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: MQM analysis
messages.body_plain:
You can get artifacts in the fit of tightly linked QTL, especially if there are phenotype outliers. This may be going on with your data.  Ideally, you want at least two markers between any two QTL, but I think even then you can get artifacts.

Also, the calculation of percent variance explained in fitqtl seems to not be appropriate for linked QTL.

karl

> Can you shed some light on why this may be and how you would interpret

>
> Thank you very much in advance.
>
> Nick

>> There are differences in how the models are fit. (That is, how the missing genotype data at putative QTL is accommodated.). The other major difference concerns the evaluation of the quality of a model (or its terms).  MQM makes use of the estimated residual SD under a "full model" with all marker covariates, while fitqtl and related functions estimate the residual SD separately for each QTL model.
